files.text:
# Seed registry for the `us-apply-rewalk-converges` BDD fixture.
#
# Engineered so that `us apply 99.3 --fix` must apply TWO fixes during
# walk #1 (one per AC), and walk #2 then verifies a clean fixpoint:
#
#   - AC 001's "present?" prompt FAILS because no entry references
#     lineage id 99.3-001-mcp-initialize. F: adds a new entry keyed by it.
#   - AC 002's "present?" prompt FAILS because no entry references
#     lineage id 99.3-002-mcp-get-refused. F: adds a new entry keyed by it.
#
# After walk #1, `anyFixApplied=true` → the engine re-walks. Walk #2
# finds AC-1 and AC-2 both present, no duplicates, all prompts pass,
# zero fixes applied → fixpoint reached → canonical commit.
#
# This is the simplest possible deterministic exercise of the
# re-walk-to-fixpoint plumbing. It avoids the
# duplicate-collapse F: path (which can take multiple Claude
# iterations to converge) and the cross-AC invalidation case (which
# depends on Claude's interpretation of "duplicate by behavior").

metadata:
  title: "Test Requirements Registry (BDD fixture seed)"
  version: "2.0"
  last_updated: "2026-05-14"
  description: "Empty seed for us-apply re-walk converges fixture"

scenarios:
  "99.3-001-mcp-initialize":
    description: "MCP server answers a valid JSON-RPC initialize POST to /mcp with HTTP 200 and a JSON-RPC envelope"
    service: ""
    path: "tests/mcp/mcp_endpoint_test.go"
    last_updated: "2026-10-21"
    user_stories:
      - story: "docs/product/stories/99.3-rewalk-fixture.yaml"
        scenario_id: "99.3-001-mcp-initialize"
        merge_date: "2026-10-21"
    merged_steps:
      given:
        - the MCP server is running on its configured port
        - the server accepts JSON-RPC over HTTP POST at /mcp
      when:
        - the Claude User posts a valid JSON-RPC initialize request to /mcp
      then:
        - the server returns HTTP 200
        - and: the response body is a well-formed JSON-RPC envelope referencing the request id
  "99.3-002-mcp-get-refused":
    description: "MCP server refuses an HTTP GET to /mcp with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed"
    service: ""
    path: "tests/mcp/mcp_endpoint_test.go"
    last_updated: "2026-10-21"
    user_stories:
      - story: "docs/product/stories/99.3-rewalk-fixture.yaml"
        scenario_id: "99.3-002-mcp-get-refused"
        merge_date: "2026-10-21"
    merged_steps:
      given:
        - the MCP server is running on its configured port
      when:
        - the Claude User sends an HTTP GET request to /mcp
      then:
        - the server returns HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed
        - and: the response indicates the method is not allowed for this endpoint
